title: "Correct Info" charges the client 2 credits and reports success even when the correction was thrown away

title: Exported PDFs silently swallow any text in angle brackets, including the templates' unfilled placeholder slots
surface: Document viewer slide-over → Export → Export PDF (print window)
whatYouSee: A client exports Brand Voice as a PDF. On screen a voice-dimension bullet reads "Formal to casual: position plus when it moves" inside angle brackets. In the printed PDF the same bullet reads "Formal to casual:" and then nothing — the bracketed text has vanished. Any line with angle-bracketed text loses that text in the export, so a partly-filled document silently loses content in exactly the file a client is most likely to forward.
whyItsWrong: The print renderer builds its HTML without ever escaping the document body — only the page title is escaped. The on-screen renderer escapes first and says why in a comment: so any angle brackets in the source text cannot break out into the surrounding structure. The print path runs the same model-written markdown with that protection removed, so the browser parses angle-bracketed text as markup and drops it. The document templates are full of angle-bracket placeholder slots, so any section the model left unfilled loses its text. A stray image or script tag reaching a document would also execute in the print window.

title: Raw markdown leaks into the document viewer: literal hash marks, orphaned nested bullets, and unrendered link syntax
surface: Document viewer slide-over — most visibly Market Strategy → Personas
whatYouSee: Inside a client-facing document you read a line that literally begins with four hash marks before the persona's name, sub-bullets that show a bare dash and sit outside the styled bullet list at the wrong indentation, and any source reference printed as square-bracket text followed by a raw address in parentheses instead of a link.
whyItsWrong: The renderer handles only two levels of heading, only bullets that start at the very beginning of a line, and has no link rule at all. A four-hash heading fails the three-hash test (the next character is a hash, not a space) and falls through to the plain-paragraph rule, so the hashes render as visible text. Indented sub-bullets fail the bullet test and become paragraphs starting with a dash. Link syntax passes through verbatim. The four-hash persona heading is not hypothetical — it is in the shipped template that generates the Market Strategy document. This is raw model formatting reaching a client inside the client's own strategy documents.

evidence: src/lib/intel/pipeline.ts — document generation writes the numbered headings as literal text
src/components/client-documents.tsx / doc-render.ts — the viewer renders headings as authored
fix: Drop the literal numbers from the generation prompt and let the viewer number sections from the heading structure, so the auto-synced block cannot shift the sequence.

title: A teammate’s real name is used as the example of a wrong fact in client-facing copy
whatYouSee: The placeholder reads: e.g. “Our pricing is $49/mo, not $99/mo” or “The founder’s name is Tomer, not John”.
whyItsWrong: It hardcodes a real Karos teammate into an example a client reads, and implies he is the founder of whichever company is looking at it.
evidence: src/components/correct-info-modal.tsx — the textarea placeholder
fix: Use a neutral example: “Our head office is in Tel Aviv, not London”.

title: A fill-in-the-blank label ships as “EVERY ___ MONTH(S)”
whatYouSee: The field label is literally “EVERY ___ MONTH(S)” with three underscores, above a number input.
whyItsWrong: The underscores are a placeholder for the value that sits in the input beside it, so the label reads as unfinished.
evidence: src/components/client-documents.tsx — the Regeneration Schedule modal labels
fix: “Repeat every” with the unit beside the input: “Repeat every [3] months”.
